personality_one_liner: A gamified, high-contrast command center where every drop of sweat translates directly into XP and rank.

spacing.rule: Use tight spacing for metric grids and lists. Avoid unnecessary empty space; keep the interface highly operational and dense.

do's: Use blur on the bottom tab bar to maintain context of scrollable lists behind it.
Use blur on sticky headers when scrolling through the day's exercise list.
dont's: Do not use glass on exercise cards or meal cards. Keep them solid surfaceSecondary for operational clarity.
Avoid glassmorphism on metric grids or data visualization components.

screens.name: Workout (Home)
screens.purpose: The daily battleground displaying today's split, allowing users to check off exercises and earn XP.

states.empty: Rest day state: hero illustration of recovery, message 'Rest Day - Recover Your Strength', and a disabled 'Workout Complete' button.
states.error: Error loading workout plan, with a 'Retry' CTA.

screens.layout: Top section: A sticky user Rank Chip (e.g., 'SILVER III') and a linear XP progress bar showing current vs next level. Below: A horizontally scrolling 7-day calendar strip (acting as the 90-day challenge micro-view). Main content: A list of today's exercises (e.g., Chest + Triceps). Each exercise is a dense row (surfaceSecondary) with text for sets/reps and a high-contrast 'Complete' button. Bottom: A sticky CTA 'Complete Full Workout (+50 XP)' locked above the bottom tab bar.

screens.name: Meals
screens.purpose: A streamlined checklist for daily nutrition to ensure the user stays on track with their diet for small XP gains.

states.empty: No meals planned for today, with an illustration of meal prep and a button to 'Generate Meal Plan'.
states.error: Failed to load meal data, with 'Retry' CTA.

screens.layout: Hero image of dark meal prep container with a vertical gradient scrim (transparent to surfaceInverse). Top overlays: 'Daily Fuel' score. Main content: A vertical list of cards for Breakfast, Lunch, Snacks (x2), and Dinner. Each card has a checkbox (circle icon). Checking it fills the circle with the success color and triggers an XP pop-up animation.

screens.name: Profile & Challenge
screens.purpose: The grand overview of the user's 90-day journey, showcasing their current rank, total XP, and overarching challenge progress.

states.empty: No challenge started. Big 'Start 90-Day Challenge' CTA.
states.error: Failed to fetch stats, with 'Retry' CTA.

screens.layout: Top section: Full-width hero banner (athletic sprinting image) with a heavy vertical scrim. Overlaying the scrim: An oversized Rank Shield/Typography (e.g., 'PLATINUM') and total XP. Below the fold: A 2-column grid of operational metrics (Workouts Completed, Meal Check-in Rate, Current Streak). Bottom section: A large progress bar mapping out the full 90-Day Challenge (e.g., 'Day 42 / 90').

hero_workout.alt: Dark cinematic gym with exercise machines

meals_bg.alt: Healthy meal prep container in dark setting

profile_banner.alt: Group of men running on outdoor track at night under stadium lights

instructions_to_main_agent: Strictly follow the Dark-First Utility personality (number 7). Do not introduce rounded playful UI, soft colors, or heavy shadows.
Implement the Rank progression heavily using the condensed Rajdhani font. Ranks are Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Diamond, Master.
For the daily workout and meal lists, use solid surfaceSecondary for the cards/rows separated by borders or spacing. Avoid glassmorphism on these operational elements.
Use Phosphor icons. Ensure icon weights match consistently across the app.

Every image used as a background MUST have a top-to-bottom vertical linear gradient scrim (transparent to >=70% surfaceInverse) to guarantee text contrast. Ensure the text sits in the darkest bottom 30-40% of the area.
For interactions: Implement instantaneous state changes for checking off exercises/meals, coupled with the specified success haptics. Gamification requires immediate responsive feedback.
Ensure the 'Complete Full Workout' primary CTA is sticky at the bottom of the screen (above the tab bar), using a solid surface container or glass fallback, not hiding behind scrollable content.
